chunks: And from him, from al-Nakha'i, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Mu'awiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man who forgot the Tawaf al-Nisa' (the women's circumambulation) until he returned to his family. He said: 'Women are not permissible to him until he visits the House and performs Tawaf. If he dies, his heir should perform it on his behalf. As for while he is alive, it is not suitable for it to be performed on his behalf. And if he forgot the throwing of the Jamarat, the two are not equal; throwing is Sunnah and Tawaf is obligatory.'
And that which indicates that it is also obligatory in the Umrah al-Mut'ah is what has been narrated:

key_terms.الْعُمْرَةِ الْمَبْتُولَةِ: Umrah al-Mut'ah, the specific type of Umrah associated with Hajj Qiran or Tamattu'
key_terms.رَمْيَ الْجِمَارِ: Throwing the Jamarat (stones at the pillars in Mina)
key_terms.سُنَّةٌ: Sunnah, a recommended but not strictly obligatory act
key_terms.طَوَافَ النِّسَاءِ: Tawaf al-Nisa', the final circumambulation of the Kaaba performed to conclude Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.يَزُورَ الْبَيْتَ: Visits the House (Kaaba), referring to the ritual of circumambulation

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a pilgrim forgets Tawaf al-Nisa' before leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the distinction between *Fard* (obligatory) and *Sunnah* acts in Hajj, specifically noting that Tawaf al-Nisa' is a mandatory pillar that prevents marital intimacy until fulfilled, whereas Jamarat throwing is a Sunnah. It establishes the principle that obligatory rituals must be performed by the pilgrim personally while alive, with only the heir compensating if death occurs, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on individual accountability in worship.
